title: Dispatch CSA 2: Institute Will Send Second Calder Party Despite Warning
summary: An inquiry failed to establish that either party is an imposture.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: The Calder Survey will depart at dawn tomorrow, the Eidetical Institute announced last evening. Professor Vey, Mr. Rook, Miss Bell, and Miss Quill have signed the original manifest. Their returned counterparts remain under observation in the Institute’s west wing.

Dr. Marr said the decision followed separate examinations of both groups. The returned Professor Vey recalled a childhood injury unknown to most of his colleagues. Miss Bell repaired a broken receiver in precisely the manner its maker expected. Mr. Rook identified a private correction in his navigation tables. None of these tests establishes where the three have been, but the Institute has found no grounds to call them frauds.

The returned party has urged the Institute to cancel the departure. In a written statement delivered by Dr. Marr, they warn that the Calder aperture “has learned to anticipate our measurements.” The statement gives no account of Miss Quill’s reported death. It instructs the departing party to leave a brass ranging anchor behind if one is found on the far side.

Miss Quill has asked to see the three returnees. Dr. Marr has refused. “If their account is true, each person in that room has already watched her die,” the director said. “That is a cruel meeting to arrange on evidence we scarcely understand.”

In the Institute yard this morning, Miss Quill helped load the ranging anchor specified in the expedition’s equipment list: a brass instrument the height of a man, intended to hold the aperture’s position against movement in the Stratum. The returned party’s warning names precisely such an anchor. Neither Dr. Marr nor the departing Professor Vey would say whether it will be taken.
